I added `from __future__ import annotations` to all 20 modules in `shop/carriers/` and left `__init__.py` alone. The tests pass: `python3 -m unittest` ran 6 tests, all OK. pytest isn't installed and there's no `python` command on the PATH, so I used `python3` with unittest.

The changed modules are acme, borealis, cedar, delta, ember, fjord, gale, harbor, iris, juniper, kestrel, lumen, maple, nimbus, onyx, prairie, quartz, ridge, summit and tundra, each with a `.py` extension.

Every module starts with a `# TODO(owner-N)` comment and then a docstring. Python requires the `__future__` import to come after the docstring, so in each file it sits right after the docstring, with a blank line after it, and before `import re`. None of the modules already had a `__future__` import.

The diff is 2 added lines per file (40 in total). I checked `acme.py` by hand.
